thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident triggered — autoscale queue backlog on inference-prod-cell-7. PagerDuty incident created: PD-2468. Link: https://pd.example/INC2468
pd-bot: PagerDuty: Triggered pager PD-2468 -> oncall@redwood.urgent (severity: high). Escalation policy: inference-hotpath.
jamie: ack — I'm on it. pulling metrics now.
jamie: checking autoscaler logs... seeing scale decisions delayed, controllers reporting provision_latency ~ 240s
anika: seeing increased 5xxs from /v1/generate in us-west-2, customer reports of timeouts.
leo: is this the same warmup drift we've seen before? any node provisioning failures?
jamie: kube events show "Insufficient capacity" + provider API 429s. autoscaler kept target but nodes not coming up.
sarah: @jamie can you run the manual hotpool spinup? runbook suggests hotpool size +3
jamie: running:
```bash
scripts/hotpool/scale-hotpool --cell inference-prod-cell-7 --delta 3 --reason "pager PD-2468 manual spinup"
```
opsbot: Command accepted — scaling hotpool +3; API request queued to provider.
leo: approx ETA for nodes? last time it was ~2m after request accepted, but provider is rate-limited now.
jamie: provider responses showing 429s, retrying with backoff. opening support ticket with cloud provider.
anika: start rerouting non-urgent traffic to lower-tier models to reduce pressure? is that safe?
mike: product: notify impacted customers? We have signup forms showing some high-traffic enterprise customers active.
sarah: recommend temporary circuit-breaker for long tail requests: set timeout 10s and return 503 quickly to avoid head-of-line blocking.
jamie: applied middleware timeout change to storefront + rolled config:
```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","timeout_ms":10000,"fallback":"503_quick"}
```
opsbot: Config rollout completed to 60% of proxy fleet.
leo: hotpool scale accepted now, nodes provisioning. kube nodes joining logs:
```
node-inference-78 joined
node-inference-79 joined
```
jamie: autoscaler metrics show queue depth trending down but still above threshold. continuing monitoring.
pd-bot: PagerDuty: PD-2468 acknowledged by jamie.
anika: I'm starting customer impact list — tagging customers with errors >= 5% in last 10m.
mike: please collect request ids and sample payloads for postmortem.
jamie: grabbing kube logs and autoscaler controller logs, will paste snippets to incident doc.
sarah: any indicators of KV cache warmup issues? that can amplify token costs and delays.
leo: kvcache hitrate low for some prefixes, but main driver here is node provisioning throttled.
jamie: mitigation status: manual hotpool +3 done, config timeout rolled, customer impact limited to a subset of long-running requests. still watching for provider throttles.
anika: updating status page: "Degraded — inference generation may experience timeouts for certain requests in us-west-2" with note we are investigating.
mike: escalate to infra lead if nodes don't stabilize in 10m.
jamie: pinging infra-leads -> @sarah @mike
opsbot: PD-2468 status: acknowledged, assigned to jamie. Escalation timer paused.
leo: timeline note for PD and postmortem: root cause likely provider-side quota/rate-limit causing autoscaler inability to provision nodes fast enough.
jamie: will collect all artifacts under /incidents/PD-2468 and follow up with RCA once stable.
anika: rolling update: queue depth below alert threshold now, 503s still present but decreasing.
jamie: marking incident as "mitigated" on status page, will keep monitoring for 30m before close.
pd-bot: PagerDuty: PD-2468 resolved.
